chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the general masses, so he said:

They are today people of truce: their lost property is returned to them, their trusts are to be fulfilled, their blood is protected, and marriage with them and inheritance from them are permissible in this state.

key_terms.أَهْلُ هُدْنَةٍ: people regarded as being under a truce or protected accord
key_terms.دِمَاؤُهُمْ: their blood, meaning their lives are inviolable
key_terms.فِي هَذَا الْحَالِ: in this present state or circumstance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dealing, marrying, and inheriting with the general Muslim masses according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal and social status of the general Muslim masses as being under a condition of truce and protected relations. It establishes practical rulings concerning their rights, including returning lost property, fulfilling trusts, safeguarding lives, and the permissibility of marriage and inheritance with them in that circumstance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4646 - Al-Alaa ibn Razin asked Abu Abdullah (as) about the the general masses (Jumhur al-Nas).
Imam (as) said: "

They are today considered people of truce. Their lost property is to be returned to them, their trusts are to be fulfilled, their blood is to be protected, and marriage with them and inheritance from them is permissible in this state."
